## Paper

Q-learning

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

Tabular temporal-difference control / Q-learning.

## Theoretical benchmark

Algorithmic benchmark: Bellman optimality control with a discrete state-action value table.

## Learning setup

Discrete observations, discrete actions, epsilon-greedy exploration, TD target, learning rate, discount factor, and repeated online updates.

## Metrics

Repo-side behavioral metrics by world plus validation that the same tabular update rule runs unchanged across worlds.

## Main result

Q-learning converges to the optimal action-values with probability 1 under reasonable conditions on learning rates and Markovian environments.

## What they prove

Q-learning converges to the optimal action-values with probability 1 under reasonable conditions on learning rates and Markovian environments.

## What they only simulate

Convergence in non-discounted, absorbing Markov environments and multiple Q-value updates per iteration are extensions not formally proven.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the performance of Q-learning in complex environments or compare it against other reinforcement learning algorithms.

## What we need to reproduce

Reproduce the method-level Q-learning obligation inside this repo: explicit discrete state/action encoding, Q-table shape, TD target, epsilon schedule, and cross-world smoke/full evidence from minds/q_learning.py; cross-world Q-learning smoke and full runs..

## How our project differs

The paper establishes a general tabular RL algorithm. This repo uses Q-learning as a controlled low-capability baseline for economic worlds rather than as a theorem-reproduction exercise.

## Implementation obligations

Discrete observation encoder; finite action set; Q-table indexed by the declared state shape; epsilon-greedy action selection; TD target reward + gamma max_a Q(s',a); no world-specific changes to the Agent interface.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

minds/q_learning.py implementation; tests that QLearningMind runs on Pricing Arena, Resource Island, Auction House, Public Goods, and Labor Market; full-run welfare/collusion/sustainability/stability outputs where available.

## Failure modes to audit

Hidden world-specific Q-learning forks; state encoders that omit economically necessary information; claiming interface generality without cross-world tests; interpreting behavior without reporting state/action discretization.

## Project code comparison

Compare Q-learning to minds/q_learning.py and the cross-world Q-learning outputs. The repo satisfies the method obligation if the same Agent update rule runs over each world's explicit discrete observation shape; it does not try to reproduce a single canonical benchmark task.
